summary: Rangers have launched an urgent review after documents on the UK Intellectual Property Office show that the club’s trademarks – including the “Ready” badge and mascot Broxi Bear – were transferred to SportsDirect.com Retail Ltd on March 25, part of the security for a £5 million loan given to the previous board. The move has raised concerns among fans, as it appears to give Newcastle United owner Mike Ashley control over Rangers’ iconic assets despite the new regime’s claim of having had no discussions with him. Chairman Dave King’s team said they are probing the transfer and will assess all contractual paperwork to determine how the trademarks were assigned.

Rangers have launched an urgent investigation after documents on the UK Intellectual Property Office show that the club’s trademarks – including the “Ready” badge and mascot Broxi Bear – are now listed under SportsDirect.com Retail Ltd, the company owned by Newcastle United chairman Mike Ashley. The ownership shift stems from security rights granted to Ashley when his firm provided a £5 million loan to the previous Rangers board in January. The club’s spokesperson said the board is reviewing all related contracts and will act swiftly to protect the Light Blues’ iconic assets.

Rangers’ new regime, led by interim chairman Paul Murray, has promised a swift review of all contractual documents, stressing that no discussions with Ashley or Sports Direct took place.

Anthony Doerr’s novel “All the Light We Cannot See,” set during the WWII bombing of Saint‑Malo, won the 2015 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction, adding to its critical acclaim and a National Book Award nomination. The same ceremony honored Stephen Adly Guirgis’s play “Between Riverside and Crazy” for drama, Elizabeth Kolbert’s “The Sixth Extinction” for general nonfiction, and a slate of works in history, biography, music, and poetry. The Pulitzers, administered by Columbia University, remain among the most prestigious awards in journalism and the arts.
